name: KRWQ
oneLiner: KRWQ is a Korean won stablecoin issued against USDC, frxUSD, and Korean Treasury Bonds; KYC-gated and not offered to South Korean residents.
collateral: Mixed reserves transitioning from USDC-only toward a target mix dominated by short-term Korean Treasury Bonds. Current composition includes USDC (Circle), Frax frxUSD, and tokenized Korean Treasury Bonds issued via Etherfuse's Stablebond framework and held in segregated, bankruptcy-remote custody at Shinhan Securities.
pegMechanism: Centralized issuance against a 100% reserve. Mint and redemption are gated to KYC-verified institutional counterparties (exchanges, market makers, OTC desks). Ethereum is the canonical mint chain; Base and other destinations share unified supply via LayerZero OFT v2. KRWQ is not offered to South Korean residents pending domestic stablecoin legislation under the Korean National Assembly.

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: KRWQ's issuer reserve endpoint reports the current reserve assets and an over-100% reserve ratio, while issuer materials describe KYC-gated centralized issuance and redemption. The KRW reference and mixed reserve assets do not make this a USD peg or an algorithmic design; it is an issuer-managed reserve claim.

jurisdiction.license: Unlicensed; designed for forthcoming Korean stablecoin legislation

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Explicit Yes retained: centralized governance metadata indicates issuer or admin control; registry links were reviewed for direct freeze, blacklist, pause, burn, or upgrade authority.

notices.title: No public audit yet
notices.message: Chainlink Proof of Reserve was integrated on June 16, 2026 and now provides automated on-chain reserve verification for KRWQ. No traditional CPA-style monthly attestation report has yet been named or published.

mintAuthority.summary: KRWQ's canonical Ethereum token is a TransparentUpgradeableProxy over a Frax-style ERC20 with an owner-managed minter set: minterMint(address,uint256) is uncapped for any address in the minters mapping, and the owner (3/5 Safe 0x56398b89) can addMinter/removeMinter at will. Two active minters are KRWTCustodianWithOracle contracts, both owned by that same Safe. Base, Polygon and Fraxtal do not run lock/unlock adapters: each is a native mint-and-burn LayerZero OFT (KRWQOFT is OFTUpgradeable; token() returns itself and approvalRequired() is false), so its owner Safe can setPeer a new trusted remote and cause unbounded KRWQ to be credited on that chain. Every deployment is a transparent proxy; on Ethereum and Base the ProxyAdmin is owned by the chain's Safe, but on Polygon and Fraxtal the ProxyAdmin is owned by a single EOA (0x9fEAB70f), which can replace the implementation unilaterally. Codex and Morph are note-only (no public RPC).

controls.label: KRWQ Ethereum owner (3/5 Safe)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25530913: KRWQ (0xc00db6b4) is a transparent proxy (EIP-1967 impl 0x350b6b5c, ProxyAdmin 0xff85d94f). Verified implementation source: contract KRWQ is ERC20Permit, ERC20Burnable, Ownable2Step, with minterMint(address,uint256) onlyMinters (calls _mint, no cap) and addMinter/removeMinter onlyOwner. owner() = Safe 0x56398b89, pendingOwner() = zero. ProxyAdmin.owner() = the same Safe. mintersArray enumerates 2 active minters, 0x5573b8db and 0x7e88ac6a, both verified KRWTCustodianWithOracle proxies whose owner() and ProxyAdmin.owner() are also Safe 0x56398b89. Safe state: getThreshold()=3, getOwners()=5, getModulesPaginated() empty, guard slot zero.
controls.capDescription: No cap. minterMint(address,uint256) is uncapped for any address in the minters mapping; addMinter(address)/removeMinter(address) are onlyOwner, so this Safe can authorize unbounded new KRWQ on the canonical chain. It also owns the Ethereum ProxyAdmin.

controls.label: KRWQ Base OFT adapter owner (3/5 Safe)
controls.evidence: At Base block 48621557: KRWQ (0x370923d3) is a transparent proxy (EIP-1967 impl 0x394b2763, ProxyAdmin 0x748e1558). The verified implementation is KRWQOFT is OFTUpgradeable; token() returns 0x370923d3 (itself) and approvalRequired() returns false, which is the native mint/burn OFT signature (an OFTAdapter would return a distinct ERC20 and true). setPeer(uint32,bytes32) is onlyOwner. owner() = Safe 0x74986f1a; ProxyAdmin.owner() is the same Safe. At Base block 48621722: getThreshold()=3, getOwners()=5 signers, getModulesPaginated() empty, guard slot zero.
controls.capDescription: No cap. KRWQ on Base is a native mint-and-burn OFT, not a lock/unlock adapter: _credit() mints on inbound receipt. The owner Safe can setPeer(uint32,bytes32) to trust a new remote source, and also owns the ProxyAdmin, so it can authorize unbounded new KRWQ on Base.

controls.label: KRWQ Polygon ProxyAdmin owner (single EOA)
controls.capDescription: Single-key upgrade authority. As sole owner of the Polygon ProxyAdmin (0x4583b85c), this EOA can call upgradeAndCall() to replace the KRWQ implementation with one that mints without limit. No cap, no timelock, no multisig.
controls.evidence: At Polygon block 90218312: the KRWQ proxy's EIP-1967 admin slot holds ProxyAdmin 0x4583b85c (OZ v5: upgradeAndCall(address,address,bytes) onlyOwner, UPGRADE_INTERFACE_VERSION present). ProxyAdmin.owner() = 0x9feab70f, and eth_getCode at that address returned 0x (no code) — a plain EOA, not a Safe. This address is also a signer on all four KRWQ Safes.

controls.label: KRWQ Fraxtal ProxyAdmin owner (single EOA)
controls.capDescription: Single-key upgrade authority. As sole owner of the Fraxtal ProxyAdmin (0x3faff366), this EOA can call upgradeAndCall() to replace the KRWQ implementation with one that mints without limit. No cap, no timelock, no multisig.
controls.evidence: At Fraxtal block 38610876: the KRWQ proxy's EIP-1967 admin slot holds ProxyAdmin 0x3faff366 (OZ v5 ProxyAdmin). ProxyAdmin.owner() = 0x9feab70f, and eth_getCode at that address returned 0x (no code) — a plain EOA, not a Safe. Same address is a signer on all four KRWQ Safes.

review.evidence: Re-verified on-chain at pinned blocks (Ethereum 25530913, Base 48621557/48621722, Polygon 90218312/90218531, Fraxtal 38610876/38611041). All four deployments are TransparentUpgradeableProxies. Ethereum: owner() = 3/5 Safe 0x56398b89 (owners and threshold re-read, no modules, guard zero); implementation KRWQ exposes uncapped minterMint() onlyMinters plus addMinter/removeMinter onlyOwner; mintersArray = 2 active KRWTCustodianWithOracle contracts, both owned by that Safe; ProxyAdmin 0xff85d94f owned by that Safe. Base/Polygon/Fraxtal are NOT lock/unlock adapters: each implementation is KRWQOFT is OFTUpgradeable with token() == self and approvalRequired() == false (native mint/burn OFT), so each owner Safe can setPeer a new trusted remote and cause unbounded credit-side minting on its chain; canRaiseCap is therefore true for all three. ProxyAdmin ownership is split: Ethereum and Base ProxyAdmins are owned by their chain Safe, but the Polygon (0x4583b85c) and Fraxtal (0x3faff366) ProxyAdmins are owned by a single EOA, 0x9feab70f (eth_getCode = 0x on both chains), which can unilaterally replace the implementation. Codex and Morph remain note-only (no public RPC).

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: KRWQ uses or is linked to LayerZero/OFT-style cross-chain token infrastructure. Because OFT/adapter routes depend on external messaging, endpoint configuration, and lock/mint or burn/mint token contracts outside issuer-native redemption alone, Pharos scores the reviewed route as external lock/mint.
